title: Tarabai
summary: Tarabai (1675–1761) led Maratha resistance to the Mughals after her husband Rajaram died in March 1700. Encyclopedia.com says she crowned her infant son Shivaji as chhatrapati at Panhala near Kolhapur and harassed Aurangzeb with guerrilla forces until his death in 1707. Historian Richard Eaton dates the anti-Mughal movement she led to 1700–1710.

as_recorded.value: Rajaram, who died on 2 March 1700 at his Sinhagad

where.modern_name: Panhala Fort, near Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India
where.historical_name: Panhala, seat of the Kolhapur branch of the Maratha state

importance.justification: Cambridge historian Richard Eaton calls her one of the most remarkable women in Indian history, leader of the 1700-1710 anti-Mughal movement.
